title: Spreadsheet import
purpose: Load the laboratory's client list from CSV files: organizations, then their sites and contacts, then the identifiers other systems (such as the LIS) use for each organization. Download a template for each file, fill it in, and import it after checking a preview.
summary: Load organizations, sites, contacts and their external identifiers from CSV files. Each file is checked before anything is saved and imports completely or not at all.

tasks.title: Load a client list for the first time
steps: Download each template from the Template column and replace its example row with your own rows.
Import [[Organizations]] first, then [[Sites]], [[Contacts]] and [[External identifiers]]: each file needs the records of the ones before.

tasks.title: Correct records in bulk
steps: Upload a file with the same keys and the corrected values. Rows that match an existing record change it; the preview shows each value before and after.

good_to_know: Only account managers, client services staff and the admin role can open import pages.
Importing the same file again changes nothing and records nothing.
The import never creates sign-in accounts or portal access, sends no email and takes no patient data.
Keys stay inside one organization: a site or contact row never moves a record to another organization.

items.label: File
items.description: Opens the import page for organizations, sites, contacts or external identifiers.

items.label: Step
items.description: The order to import in. Sites need their organizations; contacts need their organizations and the sites they serve; external identifiers need their organizations and the external systems an administrator set up.

items.label: Needs first
items.description: What must already exist in the application before the file can be imported.

items.label: Template
items.description: Downloads a CSV file with the header row and one synthetic example row, saved as UTF-8 with a byte-order mark so spreadsheet programs read accents correctly.

sections.title: Before you import
paragraphs: Files are CSV UTF-8 with the header row first, up to 1024 KiB and 2000 rows. Header names ignore letter case. A file in another encoding is refused rather than guessed. Columns that would hold patient data (such as patient_name, mrn or dob) are refused.
